group: JSON Pointer starting with "#/" – normal path

cases.expected: Returns the JsonNode located at "/properties/name" (non‑missing node). The method should not invoke handleNullNode.
cases.description: The reference begins with "#/". The leading "#" is stripped, leaving "/properties/name" which starts with "/". After URL decoding the pointer the code calls node.at("/properties/name"). The mocked node.at returns a non‑missing JsonNode, so the method returns that node directly.

group: JSON Pointer starting with "/" – missing node triggers fallback

cases.expected: Returns the fallback JsonNode produced by handleNullNode(ref, schema).
cases.description: The reference starts directly with "/". After decoding the pointer the code calls node.at("/definitions/address"). The mocked node.at returns a MissingNode, causing the method to call handleNullNode and return its result.

group: Fragment reference starting with "#" (non‑empty) – meta‑schema resolves

cases.expected: Returns the JsonNode supplied by metaSchema.getNodeByFragmentRef(ref, originalNode).
cases.description: The reference does not start with "#/" nor with "/" but matches the first part of the else‑if (starts with "#" and length > 1). The meta‑schema is asked for the fragment node and returns a non‑null node, which is then returned by the method.

group: Fragment reference starting with "urn:" – meta‑schema cannot resolve, fallback used

cases.expected: Returns the fallback JsonNode produced by handleNullNode(ref, schema).
cases.description: The reference starts with "urn:" and length > 4, satisfying the else‑if condition. metaSchema.getNodeByFragmentRef returns null, so the method calls handleNullNode and returns its result.

group: Reference with no special prefix – returns original schema node

cases.expected: Returns the original schema node (the node obtained from findAncestor().getSchemaNode()).
cases.description: The reference does not match any of the conditional prefixes, so none of the branches are taken and the method returns the original node unchanged.

cases.expected: Returns the JsonNode located at "/encoded path" after URL decoding.
cases.description: The reference begins with "#/". After stripping the leading "#" the pointer is "/encoded%20path". URLDecoder.decode converts it to "/encoded path". node.at("/encoded path") returns a non‑missing node, which is returned directly.

group: Reference equal to "#" – returns original schema node

cases.expected: Returns the original schema node obtained from findAncestor().getSchemaNode() because the reference does not satisfy any of the conditional branches (length is not > 1).
cases.description: The reference consists of only a hash character. The method should skip the "#/" and "#" fragment handling blocks and fall through, returning the unchanged original node.

group: Empty string reference – returns original schema node

cases.expected: Returns the original schema node (the node obtained from findAncestor().getSchemaNode()).
cases.description: An empty string does not match any prefix checks, so the method should simply return the original node.

group: JSON Pointer starting with "/" – normal (non‑missing) node

cases.expected: Returns the JsonNode located at "/properties/age" (non‑missing node). The method should not invoke handleNullNode.
cases.description: The reference begins directly with "/". After URL decoding the pointer, node.at("/properties/age") returns a valid JsonNode, so the method returns it directly.

group: Reference starting with "urn:" but exactly 4 characters – falls back to original node

cases.expected: Returns the original schema node because the length check (ref.length() > 4) fails, so the branch is not taken.
cases.description: Although the string starts with "urn:", its length is not greater than 4, therefore the method treats it as a plain reference and returns the original node.

group: JSON Pointer with "#/" prefix that resolves to a missing node – fallback via handleNullNode

cases.expected: Returns the fallback JsonNode produced by handleNullNode(ref, schema) because node.at("/nonexistent") yields a MissingNode.
cases.description: The reference starts with "#/". After stripping the leading "#" the pointer becomes "/nonexistent". The call to node.at returns a MissingNode, triggering the fallback logic.

group: JSON Pointer with URL‑encoded slash (%2F) inside the path

cases.expected: Returns the JsonNode located at "/components/schemas/User" after URL decoding the "%2F" sequences.
cases.description: The reference begins with "#/" and contains URL‑encoded forward slashes. After decoding, the pointer becomes "/components/schemas/User"; node.at should be invoked with this decoded pointer and its result returned.

cases.expected: Throws NullPointerException because the method dereferences the argument with startsWith().
cases.description: Passing a null reference should cause the first call to ref.startsWith(...) to throw a NullPointerException, which is the expected behavior for this edge case.

cases.expected: Throws NullPointerException because findAncestor() returns null and the subsequent call to schema.getSchemaNode() dereferences a null reference.
cases.description: The method starts by calling findAncestor(). If the mocked JsonSchema instance is set up so that findAncestor() returns null, the next line `schema.getSchemaNode()` will cause a NullPointerException before any other logic (prefix checks, URL decoding, etc.) is executed.

group: schema.getSchemaNode returns null – NullPointerException on node.at

cases.expected: Throws NullPointerException because schema.getSchemaNode() returns null and the method attempts to invoke `node.at(jsonPointer)` on a null JsonNode.
cases.description: The reference begins with "#/" so the method will strip the leading "#" and enter the JSON‑Pointer branch. The node variable is obtained from `schema.getSchemaNode()`. If that call is mocked to return null, the subsequent `node.at(jsonPointer)` dereferences a null object, producing a NullPointerException.

cases.expected: Throws NullPointerException because schema.getSchemaNode() returns null and the method attempts to invoke `node.at(jsonPointer)` on a null JsonNode.
cases.description: A reference that starts directly with "/" also triggers the JSON‑Pointer branch. With `schema.getSchemaNode()` mocked to null, the call to `node.at(jsonPointer)` results in a NullPointerException.

group: metaSchema is null – NullPointerException on fragment resolution

cases.expected: Throws NullPointerException because the JsonSchema instance's metaSchema field is null and the method attempts to call `metaSchema.getNodeByFragmentRef(...)`.
cases.description: The reference starts with "#" and has length > 1, so the method enters the fragment‑reference branch. If the `metaSchema` dependency is mocked (or left unset) to be null, the call `this.metaSchema.getNodeByFragmentRef(ref, node)` dereferences a null reference, causing a NullPointerException.

cases.expected: Throws NullPointerException because the JsonSchema instance's metaSchema field is null and the method attempts to call `metaSchema.getNodeByFragmentRef(...)`.
cases.description: The reference starts with "urn:" and length > 4, so the same fragment‑reference branch is taken. With `metaSchema` null, the method throws a NullPointerException when invoking `getNodeByFragmentRef`.
